title: How tall can your fence be? Check these first

headline: HOW TALL CAN
YOUR *FENCE* BE?
beats.vo: How tall can your fence be? It depends where it goes, and on your city.

headline: *~4 FT* FRONT,
*~6 FT* BACK
beats.vo: In most Lower Mainland cities it's about *four feet* in the front yard and about *six* in the back. Every city is different.

headline: CORNER LOT?
*LOWER* LIMITS
beats.vo: *Corner lots* have a sightline zone near the corner where fences and hedges stay around *one metre*.

headline: FENCE ON A WALL?
IT CAN *ADD UP*
beats.vo: Putting a fence on a *retaining wall*? Some cities count them *together*.

headline: PROPERTY LINE?
*GET A SURVEY*
beats.vo: And only a *B.C. Land Surveyor* can confirm your property line.

post.caption: How tall can your fence be in the Lower Mainland? Height limits are typically about 4 ft in front yards and 6 ft in back, corner lots are lower near the corner, and in some cities a fence on a retaining wall counts as one combined height. Check your city's bylaw before you build; only a BC Land Surveyor can confirm your property line.
post.alt: A black steel privacy fence along a lawn, animated diagrams of typical front and back yard fence heights, a corner-lot sightline and a fence on a retaining wall, and a wood-grain metal fence with a slat topper.
